extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (ECRs), potential mentors, journal editors, and organizers interested in peer-review training and inclusive reviewer recruitment
extracted.subtask_description: Description of PREreview's Open Reviewers program and live-streamed preprint journal clubs: goals, structure, stage-based progression, outputs, and diversity/inclusion selection practices for training early-career researchers to write constructive, equitable open peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train ECRs to write constructive manuscript reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Train ECRs on how to write constructive manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program goal: provide training so early-career researchers learn how to write constructive manuscript reviews and build open-review profiles (published reviews on PREreview.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and combat biases / systems of oppression in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Train ECRs to recognize and combat biases, and understand systems of oppression as they manifest within the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum focus includes understanding how systems of oppression manifest within the scientific enterprise and helping mentees recognize and challenge their own internal biases that may influence objectivity when reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairing mentees with experienced mentors and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Pair ECRs with more experienced reviewers and journal editors who provide mentorship and constructive feedback to writing manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship is a core element: stage-based pairings (e.g., RTs with RMs in cohort component; ARTs with ARs in self-guided component) include one-to-one calls and feedback on writing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to a support network of peers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Help ECRs access a support network of peers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program activities (community calls, peer-to-peer support chats) are designed to build networks and peer support in addition to mentor relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase racial diversity in the reviewer pool (pilot quota)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help bring more racial diversity to the peer reviewer pool — in the pilot we reserved 50% of the mentee slots to applicants who self-identified as underrepresented racial minorities as defined by the National Science Foundation (NSF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot selection explicitly reserved half of mentee slots for NSF-defined underrepresented racial minorities; the program acknowledges this is a US-centric definition and aims to expand definitions as it grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a database of trained reviewers for editorial prospecting
rubrics_metrics.description: Work together with the mentors to build a database of trained reviewers that journal editors can easily access when selecting reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon meeting completion/quality thresholds, participants are added to a Trained Reviewer list intended for editorial prospecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 (Review Trainees, RTs) completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 Review Trainees are researchers with little-to-no experience; upon completion, RTs will have published 2 preprint reviews on PREreview.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of stage 1 prepares RTs to join stage 2 if they wish; stage 1 is delivered via the 14-week cohort-based component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 (Advanced Review Trainees, ARTs) entry and completion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ARTs have completed 2–5 manuscript reviews previously and, upon completion of the self-guided component, will have published an additional 4 preprint reviews on PREreview.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With a total of 6 highly scored manuscript reviews (prior reviews + new ones), ARTs will be added to the Trained Reviewer list for editorial prospecting and qualify to join stage 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3 (Advanced Reviewers, ARs) role and completion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: ARs have completed at least 6 manuscript reviews and want to learn more about implicit bias and mentoring; upon completion they will be added to the Trained Reviewer list (if not already) and qualify to join stage 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 3 focuses on implicit bias, systems of oppression, and building mentoring skills by supporting ARTs in the self-guided component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 4 (Review Mentors, RMs) role and entry expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 4 Review Mentors are experienced reviewers (e.g., journal editors) who have completed stage 3 or enter with extensive peer review experience; they are willing to mentor RTs in the cohort-based component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RMs engage in mentorship, help RTs learn about implicit bias and systems of oppression, and volunteer time to train cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program format and durations (cohort-based and self-guided)
rubrics_metrics.description: To allow different levels and paces of engagement, the program has a 14-week cohort-based component (stages 1 and 4) and an 8-month self-guided component (stages 2 and 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cohort-based is interactive with scheduled community events; self-guided provides recorded materials plus monthly mentor calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort-based activities and curriculum focus
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 14-week cohort, RTs engage in community calls, peer-to-peer support chats, and one-to-one RTs/RMs calls; the curriculum focuses on critical evaluation of emerging scientific literature, strategies to write constructive reviews, understanding systems of oppression, and recognizing/challenging internal biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provides mentorship and leadership training for mentees who wish to become future mentors; these activities aim to produce published preprint reviews and review skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-guided component mechanics and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 8-month self-guided component ARTs access recorded videos, documents, and resources; are paired with ARs for monthly 30–60 minute calls; and, with mentor support, complete and publish 4 preprint reviews on PREreview.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARs are expected to watch a recorded Mentor Thought Exercise before their first one-to-one call to encourage a supportive, nurturing, and safe mentoring environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor expectations and supportive mentorship practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors should provide constructive feedback, create a supportive/nurturing/safe space, and help mentees develop peer reviewing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor Thought Exercise exists to model supportive mentoring; mentors (RMs/ARs) are tasked with leadership and mentoring training responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold: 'highly scored' manuscript reviews as trigger for Trained Reviewer list
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants with a total of 6 highly scored manuscript reviews will be added to a Trained Reviewer list for editorial prospecting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'highly scored' implies reviews are evaluated for quality, though the page does not provide a numeric scoring rubric; the count threshold (six) is explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reviews openly on PREreview.org to build open reviewer profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Program expects participants to publish preprint reviews on PREreview.org as part of building open peer review profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage completion and Trained Reviewer listing depend on publication of reviews on PREreview.org; open publication supports integration with journal review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-streamed preprint journal clubs: structured facilitation and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Live-streamed preprint journal clubs are topic-centered events that follow guided discussion questions encouraging diverse participation; after the call the discussion is summarized into a peer review report openly shared on PREreview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitation roles include two PREreview facilitators (experienced), optional topic expert, optional preprint authors, and participating researchers; outputs can be integrated into journal-organized peer review (example: PREreview included as reviewer #3 in eLife process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guided discussion questions to encourage diverse participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use guided discussion questions in live-streamed journal clubs to encourage diverse methods of participation and structured, constructive discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions and structure are intended to empower underrepresented researchers and early-career participants to contribute meaningfully during journal clubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and pilot implementation constraints and future intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot launched Oct 2020 with limited applications and slots (selected numbers given); pilot mainly accommodated U.S. and European applicants and used NSF definition of underrepresented racial minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program acknowledges its North American/life-sciences developer bias and commits to adapt curriculum and definitions to be more globally inclusive as it expands and partners with like-minded organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output integration expectation for journal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports produced by journal clubs are openly shared on PREreview and can be integrated into journal-organized peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example given where a PREreview report was included as reviewer #3 in the eLife peer review process for a bioRxiv preprint.
